resumen.aldeanosNota: Amounts are indicative: the game rolls each trade price within a range, and it drops permanently if you cure the villager from being a zombie. Open a profession to see all of its trades.
mob.ultimoBloque: Place {bloque} last. It does not come alive until that piece is on, and the moment it is, everything starts: step back.

portada.subtitulo: And land on everything related at once, without searching again.
nombres.subtitulo: Type a name and copy it in letters the game can actually draw. None of the fancy letters other sites give you: those show up as white boxes inside Minecraft.
nombres.cuidado: Name it in the same go as the first book
nombres.cuidadoTexto: Renaming uses up an anvil go just like enchanting, and every go makes the next ones dearer. Naming it in a separate operation can cost you many extra levels: on a four-step pickaxe it is eight. Type the name in the same operation where you add the first book and it costs one.
encantador.subtitulo: Pick what you want to enchant and which enchantments you want. We tell you in what order to combine them so it comes out as cheap as possible.
tintes.subtitulo: Put dyes in the grid and see what colour comes out. If nothing does, we tell you what is missing. Below are all 16 dyes, where each one comes from and what it mixes with.
tintes.pruebaAyuda: Tap a dye to put it in the grid. Tap a slot to take it out. Mixing happens in your inventory, no crafting table needed.
tintes.vacio: The grid is empty. Tap a dye to start.
tintes.nada: That makes nothing. Add another dye or take one out.
tintes.lleno: These four make nothing. Take one out.
tintes.todosAyuda: Some dyes only come from flowers and things you find around the world. The rest can also be mixed. If you cannot find a flower, check here for another way.
tintes.paraQueTexto: A dye changes the colour of wool, beds, glass, terracotta, candles, shulker boxes and your dogs’ and cats’ collars. It also dyes leather armour: add several dyes at once and the colours blend. And at the loom you use them to draw on banners.
telar.subtitulo: Pick the cloth, the dye and the patterns, and see how your banner looks. We tell you what to bring to the loom and in what order.
telar.lleno: You have 6 layers, the loom’s limit
telar.paso3: 3. Tap a pattern to add it
telar.paso3Ayuda: Each pattern is a layer painted over the ones before. The buttons already show how it looks with the dye you picked.
telar.leyendaItem: This pattern only shows up if you put its banner pattern in the loom.
telar.pasos: Step by step at the loom
telar.entreCapas: Between one layer and the next, take the banner out of the right slot and put it back in the first one.
telar.noSeGasta: Not used up: the loom gives it back
telar.pasoBase: Put the {estandarte} in the first slot of the loom.
telar.pasoCapa: Put {tinte} in the second slot and pick {patron}.
telar.pasoCapaItem: Put {tinte} in the second slot and {item} in the third. Then pick {patron}.
telar.pasoFinal: Take the banner out of the right slot. Done!
telar.pasoSinCapas: Tap a pattern above to see the steps.
telar.truco.escudoTexto: Put the shield and the banner together in a crafting table. The shield gets the design and the banner is used up. It only works on a shield with no design yet.
telar.truco.copiarTexto: Put your banner and a blank banner of the same colour in a crafting table. You get both back with the design, no dyes needed.
telar.truco.quitarTexto: Use the banner on a cauldron with water and the last layer you added comes off. Each time uses some water. It does not work in Bedrock.
telar.truco.limiteTexto: The loom lets you add up to six patterns. If you want something more detailed, think about which layers cover each other and drop the ones you cannot see.
telar.conPatron: Patterns that need a banner pattern
telar.conPatronTexto: Most patterns are always there in the loom. These are not: to make them show up you put their banner pattern in the third slot. It is not used up, so one is enough forever.
telar.faltaTinte: Missing a colour? See how to get it or how to mix it.
encantador.paso3: How many times has it been through the anvil?
encantador.trabajosAyuda: If the item is new, or you only enchanted it at the table, leave the zero. Count the times you repaired it or gave it a name too: renaming uses up an anvil trip just like enchanting, and every previous trip makes all the next ones dearer.
encantador.renombrar: I am going to name it
encantador.renombrarAyuda: Renaming costs one level. Doing it in a separate operation counts as another anvil go and makes every later step dearer: on a four-step route that is about eight extra levels.
encantador.conNombre: Type the name here too, in this same operation.
encantador.elige: Pick at least one enchantment to calculate.
encantador.pico: The dearest single step is {n} levels: have at least that many before you start.
encantador.pasoObjeto: Put {objeto} on the left and {libro} on the right
encantador.pasoLibros: Put {a} on the left and {b} on the right
encantador.demasiadoCaro: There is no way to get all of that: some combination would go over 39 levels and the anvil would refuse it. Try dropping an enchantment, or splitting it across two items.
encantador.comoLeer: Each step is one anvil operation. The penalty grows with every one, which is why the order matters as much as the enchantments.
